links.note: The raw list 1,1,2,4,3,2,1,2,2,4 has to be tallied into counts before the most frequent value (2, four times) can be named. Turning raw figures into an organised count is this concept; nothing here is graphed.

It is the bar's height/length, not its breadth, that carries the information - the uniform-width, proportional-height definition of a bar graph, stated in this concept as 'uniform width is what makes height alone carry the comparison'.
One symbol worth 100 flowers means 800 flowers need 8 symbols. Knowing what a single symbol is worth is exactly what this concept says reading a pictograph requires.
A full tally group stands for a frequency of 5. Tally marks are the systematic organising step that turns collected figures into a frequency, which is this concept.
